question: How much does it cost to install hardwood stair treads?
title: Cost to Install Hardwood Stair Treads (2026)
h1: What Do Hardwood Stair Treads Cost Installed?
description: Hardwood stair treads run $130-$220 per tread installed in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026, with risers adding $25-$65 each per step.
capsule: Hardwood stair treads typically run $130-$220 per tread installed in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026, with risers adding $25-$65 each. A 13-step staircase runs roughly $1,700-$2,900 for treads alone. National averages from HomeGuide and Angi land close, around $100-$250 per step installed.

sections.h2: What hardwood stair treads cost installed in 2026
sections.html:
A single solid hardwood tread, installed, runs $130-$220 in our Sarasota and Manatee County market. That price covers the tread itself, fastening to the stair stringer, and finish work to match your existing hardwood or the new floor at the top and bottom of the stairs. Risers - the vertical boards between treads - are priced separately, typically $25-$65 each, and not every staircase gets them replaced if the existing risers are painted trim rather than flooring material.

sections.h2: What changes the price per step
sections.html:
Wood species is the biggest swing - a red oak tread costs less than a wide-plank white oak tread cut to match a herringbone floor at the top of the stairs. Nosing profile matters too: a bullnose or waterfall edge takes more shop time than a square-edge tread. Winder stairs, the pie-shaped treads on a turning staircase, cost more per step than a straight run because each one is measured and cut individually rather than from a standard template.

National data lines up with what we see locally. HomeGuide puts hardwood stairs at $100-$250 per step installed, with installers charging $50-$80 an hour separately for custom work like winders. Angi's number is close, around $160 per step, or roughly $1,600-$1,920 for a 10-12 step flight with labor included. A U-shaped or L-shaped staircase with a landing typically costs more overall than a straight run of the same total step count, simply because the landing itself needs its own flooring treatment and trim detail where it meets the treads.

sections.h2: Why hardwood is still the common choice for stair treads
sections.html:
Even in a house getting LVP or laminate throughout the main floor, stairs are usually the one place we still recommend hardwood or engineered treads. Resilient flooring doesn't have a reliable stair-nose profile in most product lines, and glued-on vinyl or laminate nosings tend to come loose from the constant flex of foot traffic on an edge. A hardwood tread stained to match the rest of the floor solves that without the maintenance problem.

Florida Residential Code R311.7.5 requires stair nosing between 3/4 in. and 1-1/4 in. on stairs with solid risers, and hardwood treads are milled to that spec as a standard part of the tread, not an add-on piece that can work loose. Skirt boards, the trim running along the wall side of an open staircase, are worth budgeting for at the same time - repainting or replacing them once treads are finished is far more efficient than coming back for a second trip.

sections.h2: What's included in a written stair tread quote
sections.html: Our estimates break a staircase job into treads, risers, nosing profile and any skirt board work as separate lines, the same way we itemize material, labor, removal and prep on a flooring job. If you're replacing carpet on the stairs, add the cost of pulling the old carpet and pad and checking the stringer underneath for squeaks or damage before the new treads go on - that's a common surprise on a staircase that hasn't been opened up in twenty or thirty years. A 13-step staircase, common in a two-story Lakewood Ranch or Parrish floor plan, typically runs $1,700-$2,900 for treads alone before risers and nosing are added in. Send us a photo of your staircase through our free estimate form and we'll price it out step by step.

faqs.q: Do stair treads have to match the flooring at the top and bottom of the stairs?
faqs.a: Not exactly, but most customers pick a stain or plank width close enough that the transition reads as intentional rather than mismatched. We bring samples to the estimate to compare against your existing or planned floor.

faqs.q: Can I install engineered hardwood treads instead of solid?
faqs.a: Yes, and it typically costs $110-$180 per tread installed versus $130-$220 for solid. Just confirm the wear layer thickness, since stairs get heavier point-load traffic than open floor.

faqs.q: How long does it take to install treads on a typical staircase?
faqs.a: A straight run of 12-14 steps usually takes one to two days, longer if winders or a full stair remodel with new risers and skirt boards is part of the job.
